title: Empowering the Clinical Management of BMFs Through a Biological and Genetically Driven Pediatric and Adult National Network
official: Potenziare la Gestione Clinica Delle CMF Attraverso Una Rete Nazionale Pediatrica e Dell'Adulto Basata su Dati Biologici e Genetici / Empowering the Clinical Management of BMFs Through a Biological and Genetically Driven Pediatric and Adult National Network
summary:
A non-profit, translational, prospective and retrospective study.

Patients will be enrolled according to the procedures described in the protocol, and samples will be processed and analyzed as specified in the protocol.

Since constitutional bone marrow failure syndromes (CMF) are rare genetic disorders characterized by a variable and incompletely defined clinical phenotype, a partially unknown genetic etiology, and pathogenetic mechanisms that are only partly understood, the investigators hypothesize that a number of patients currently diagnosed with idiopathic acquired aplastic anemia (AAA) or idiopathic single-lineage/multilineage bone marrow failure (BMF) may have been misdiagnosed and may actually have an underlying CMF.

Therefore, the investigators' primary objective is to identify CMF underlying BMF and vice versa, by defining well-characterized patient cohorts based on clinical and family history, clinical manifestations, and immunological findings; identifying disease-specific parameters and biomarkers; and providing disease-specific guidelines to facilitate early diagnosis and, consequently, enable timely and appropriate treatment.

In this context, the use of appropriate artificial intelligence (AI) tools is likely to improve the diagnostic accuracy of this approach.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients diagnosed with Fanconi anemia (FA), dyskeratosis congenita (DC) and other telomere biology disorders (TBD), congenital neutropenia (CN), primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRD), congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (CAMT), and acquired aplastic anemia (AAA), with or without paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).
* Signed informed consent and/or assent obtained from the participant and/or their parents or legal guardians, as applicable.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Absence of signed informed consent and/or assent from the participant and/or their parents or legal guardians
